paragraphs: The 318d has been a mainstay of the 3 Series diesel range since 2012, spanning two generations under one badge. Early F30/F31 cars (2012–2015) use the N47 — a 2.0-litre diesel known for the timing chain issue described above. From 2015, the F30/F31 generation switched to the B47, a revised 2.0-litre diesel that's significantly more reliable, and this engine carried over to the G20/G21 generation which launched in 2019. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and the known wear pattern differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 318d is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre diesel fitted to the 318d from 2012 to 2015. Known for timing chain failure due to chain guide wear, subject to NHTSA recall 18V-755 — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, guides, tensioners and gaskets as standard on every N47 rebuild.

A 2.0-litre diesel fitted from 2015 onwards. This is a revised engine that's significantly more reliable than the N47, without the same timing chain issues. We replace timing chain, bearings and gaskets as standard on every B47 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because BMW 318d can use the N47 or B47 engine code, fitting the wrong replacement risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N47 or B47) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 318d quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
